method: Primary-source web audit; scope and access boundaries in each entry.

sources.title: FPGA Accelerated Low-Latency Market Data Feed Processing
sources.publisher: Morris, Thomas and Luk / IEEE HoTI
sources.highlight: A layered FPGA feed processor parses and filters network traffic before delivering messages to host memory. It also handles redundant feeds. This establishes that the broad idea predates this project.
sources.apply: Sketch the layer boundaries and compare its measurement endpoints to yours. Its gigabit, FAST and PCIe system is related work, not a directly comparable 10G tick-to-trade baseline.

sources.title: Corundum: An Open-Source 100-Gbps NIC
sources.highlight: Corundum combines FPGA networking with queues, DMA and a host driver. Its system-level evaluation is useful beyond trading applications.
sources.apply: Study module boundaries, ownership and evaluation structure. Your Ethernet endpoint does not become a SmartNIC merely by resembling its parser; PCIe/DMA/driver integration is outside the core scope.

sources.title: P4-compatible High-level Synthesis of Low Latency 100 Gb/s Streaming Packet Parsers in FPGAs
sources.highlight: The work explores generated streaming-parser architectures and evaluates latency and resource tradeoffs on a different FPGA and link speed.
sources.apply: Use it to develop questions about parser structure, not to copy latency numbers. Your experiment compares two hand-written RTL architectures at equal semantics; publication novelty still needs a broader review.
sources.confidence: Primary research preprint; not a validated baseline for this board

sources.title: Userspace I/O HOWTO
sources.section: How UIO works; mappings and interrupts
sources.highlight: UIO can expose memory-mapped device regions and interrupts through a small kernel component and userspace control. It is not a replacement for every kernel subsystem.
sources.apply: Use it as a candidate for custom PL control registers on the onboard processor, with driver/device-tree setup and validated register ordering.

sources.title: Hardware Engineer Internship, Summer 2027
sources.highlight: The role connects SystemVerilog design with Python modeling and testing; HDL, programming, and Linux matter. UVM or cocotb experience is a bonus.
sources.apply: Produce a verified block, an independent model, and a reproducible Linux regression you can explain. Do not wait for the year-long project to finish before applying.

sources.title: FPGA Engineer
sources.highlight: The experienced role names HDL, C/C++, verification, synthesis, and timing/area constraints. Hardware bring-up is relevant.
sources.apply: Keep a critical-path explanation and post-route evidence beside your RTL. These are direction-setting skills, not a claim that an internship requires experienced-engineer mastery.

sources.title: Hardware Engineer, Chicago
sources.highlight: This ASIC-focused listing asks for SystemVerilog, verification, C++, CDC, Ethernet, and Python/Bash automation.
sources.apply: Make the hardware/software boundary explicit. This source supports transferable skills; it is not evidence that this particular job is an FPGA internship.

sources.title: ASIC Verification Engineer, GPU
sources.highlight: The indexed official description names golden models, randomized stimulus, UVM, functional coverage, assertions, and C++.
sources.apply: For ASIC verification applications, add one focused UVM environment and explain coverage closure. FPGA project relevance is an inference, not employer endorsement.
sources.confidence: Official indexed text; live application availability unverified

sources.title: KR260 Robotics Starter Kit
sources.highlight: One SFP+ cage supports a 10G path. The four RJ45 interfaces are 1G. AMD lists $349 MSRP and a 26-week lead time; distributor stock and delivered price are unverified.
sources.apply: Use a single full-duplex port: the host sends market data and receives intents over the same cable. Obtain current board, NIC, cable, and licensing quotes before purchase.
sources.confidence: Official listing; not a stock guarantee

sources.title: Soft IP for Kria Notes
sources.highlight: The KR260 SFP+ can be used from programmable logic through GTH transceivers. The listed serial-IP options do not include a turnkey example design.
sources.apply: Audit the exact carrier schematic, GT site, reference clock, SFP controls, and XDC. A board feature does not supply the integration automatically.

sources.title: KR260 BIST device-tree source
sources.highlight: The source contains an xxv-ethernet node, BASE-R configuration, DMA, and an SFP-associated clk_156 reference.
sources.apply: Use BIST as a hardware baseline. This file alone does not establish a working custom bitstream, exact oscillator routing, or MAC entitlement. Pin a known release and rebuild it.
sources.confidence: Source contents verified; hardware operation unverified

sources.title: PG210: License Type
sources.highlight: BASE-R PCS/PMA is included without an additional IP fee. The MAC and MAC+PCS features require separate fee-based licensing.
sources.apply: Choose a licensed AMD stack or a compatible open implementation. Verify unrestricted bitstream generation; a time-limited evaluation cannot establish a permanent lab setup.

sources.title: UG973: Feature Availability by Subscription Tier
sources.highlight: Basic limits XSIM size and ILA probes, and excludes IBERT and some debug flows. Device support and IP licensing are separate questions.
sources.apply: Confirm the actual university or kit entitlement before choosing a debug workflow. Older Vivado licenses may follow different rules; pin the board-supported release.

sources.title: 10G/25G High Speed Ethernet Subsystem
sources.section: RX AXI4-Stream; Frame reception with errors; Clocking
sources.highlight: The documented RX interface signals a bad frame at its final transfer. RX/TX clocking and flow-control capabilities depend on configuration.
sources.apply: Keep tentative parsing separate from committed state. Read the guide matching the generated IP version. Budget any real RX-to-core or core-to-TX clock crossing.
sources.confidence: Official versioned IP guide; match your instance

sources.title: AMBA AXI-Stream Protocol Specification
sources.highlight: Transfers happen when TVALID and TREADY are both asserted at a clock edge. The producer retains valid data while stalled and cannot wait for ready before asserting valid.
sources.apply: Advance counters only on accepted beats. Hold data, keep, last, and user metadata during a stall. Test the final beat under backpressure.
sources.quote: For a transfer to occur, both TVALID and TREADY must be asserted.

sources.title: RFC 768: User Datagram Protocol
sources.highlight: UDP length includes the eight-byte header. The checksum covers a pseudoheader and payload with odd-byte padding. For IPv4, transmitted zero means no checksum; computed zero is encoded as all ones.
sources.apply: Document whether checksum omission is accepted or rejected by project policy. Test both cases separately from a genuinely bad checksum.

sources.title: RFC 791: Internet Protocol
sources.highlight: Header length, total length, fragmentation flags, and fragment offset affect packet interpretation. The header checksum is distinct from the UDP checksum.
sources.apply: First support only IPv4 IHL=5 and unfragmented UDP. Drop and count options, fragments, unsupported protocols, and inconsistent lengths. This is a declared subset, not a complete IP stack.

sources.title: MoldUDP64 Specification
sources.section: Downstream packet header; Message block; Heartbeat
sources.highlight: Packets have a 10-byte session, 64-bit sequence, message count, and length-prefixed messages. A packet can contain multiple messages; count 0 and 0xFFFF have special meanings.
sources.apply: Build transport framing before ITCH decoding. Sequence accounting follows messages, not packets. Test a later malformed message, duplicates, gaps, and session changes.

sources.title: TotalView-ITCH 5.0 Specification
sources.section: Data Types; Add / Execute / Cancel / Delete / Replace; Trading Action
sources.highlight: ITCH is an order-event feed. Price(4) uses four implied decimal places; timestamps use six bytes. Directory, order lifecycle, and trading status affect usable state.
sources.apply: Your 31-byte bid/ask snapshot is a synthetic protocol. An ITCH book needs order-ID state and lifecycle support, bounded capacity, and recovery. Start with a declared decode-only subset before claiming a reconstructed book.

sources.title: SoupBinTCP 3.0 Specification
sources.highlight: Logical messages can be split or combined by TCP. Login, sequencing, heartbeat, and reconnection belong to the session layer.
sources.apply: Do not label a custom UDP order intent as exchange connectivity. If you later implement a host session, test partial reads, coalesced messages, reconnects, and unknown order outcome.

sources.title: OUCH 5.0 Specification
sources.section: Architecture; Enter / Cancel; Accepted / Executed / Rejected
sources.highlight: OUCH describes order entry and order lifecycle responses. An encoded message is only one part of a session and execution system.
sources.apply: Call core output OrderIntent-v1. Add an OUCH encoder only as a later compatibility exercise with a simulated venue and documented transport. No live trading is needed.

sources.title: RFC 1982: Serial Number Arithmetic
sources.highlight: Modulo sequence comparisons have an ambiguous half-range case. Ordinary integer comparison is insufficient across wrap.
sources.apply: Use these arithmetic principles for the custom 32-bit sequence scheme and declare its half-range policy. Do not assume this RFC defines Nasdaq session semantics.

sources.title: cocotb Simulator Support
sources.highlight: The documented minimum is Verilator 5.036 or Icarus 11.0. Coverage and waveform options are simulator-specific. XSim is not listed as an upstream integration.
sources.apply: Use cocotb to drive your portable RTL. Keep vendor-IP/XSim tests as a separate SV flow unless you deliberately validate another integration.

sources.title: cocotb Timing Model
sources.section: Values Change / Values Settle / End of Time Step
sources.highlight: An edge trigger can resume a test before all dependent HDL values settle. ReadOnly marks the stable observation phase.
sources.apply: Drive away from the sampling edge; await RisingEdge and then ReadOnly before checking registered outputs. Add timeouts so a missing response fails instead of hanging.

sources.title: cocotb Release Notes
sources.highlight: The release notes list 2.1.0; its new pytest regression plugin is experimental. The retrieved documentation banner still contains a development suffix.
sources.apply: Candidate: released cocotb 2.1.0, Python 3.12, and Verilator 5.052. Pin exact packages after a smoke test. The audit did not execute this pairing.

sources.title: Verilator Input Languages
sources.highlight: Verilator is mostly two-state; assertion and covergroup support is partial. It cannot simulate encrypted vendor RTL.
sources.apply: Separate portable core tests from vendor models. Run reset/X tests on a four-state simulator. Use selected assertions and verify they actually fire.

sources.title: Verilator Revision History
sources.highlight: 5.052 announces UVM 2020-3.2 support with limitations. Earlier advice that Verilator cannot run any UVM is now too broad.
sources.apply: UVM remains a later focused lane. Test its exact library and simulator combination; do not equate this release announcement with full commercial VIP compatibility.

sources.title: UG900: UVM Support
sources.highlight: XSim documents a precompiled UVM 1.2 library. This differs from the UVM 2020-3.2 version in the Verilator announcement.
sources.apply: A small UVM risk-gate bench can use an available supported simulator. Keep the cocotb baseline portable and record library versions separately.

sources.title: SBY: Formal Extensions to Verilog
sources.highlight: assert, assume, and cover serve different roles. $past is undefined at the first sample; a bounded check is not an unbounded proof.
sources.apply: Start with FIFO occupancy and no-order-while-disarmed properties. Guard initial history, review assumptions, and reach cover points. Advanced SVA support depends on the frontend.

sources.title: UG894: Non-Project Tcl Flow
sources.highlight: A scripted flow reads HDL and XDC, synthesizes, places, routes, and emits reports/checkpoints.
sources.apply: Write scripts/build.tcl plus a report checker. Fail on missing constraints, unacceptable timing, DRCs, or absent artifacts; generating a report does not mean it passed.

sources.title: UG949: Clock Domain Crossing
sources.highlight: Crossing clocks requires an appropriate structure and constraints. A multi-bit payload cannot be made coherent by synchronizing each bit independently.
sources.apply: Use vendor CDC primitives or a verified async FIFO where clocks differ. Keep an explicit clock map, reset-release policy, and reviewed CDC reports.

sources.title: RFC 2544: Benchmarking Methodology
sources.section: 9.1 Frame sizes / 24 Trial duration / 26 Throughput and latency
sources.highlight: The methodology varies Ethernet frame size and distinguishes throughput and latency measurements. It includes longer final trials.
sources.apply: Adapt its traffic sweep, not a claim of RFC compliance. Test 64 through 1518-byte ingress handling, plus 77-byte valid synthetic quotes, bursts, drops, and long runs.

sources.title: verilog-ethernet
sources.highlight: The repository is superseded by Taxi. It remains a useful version-pinned reference for Ethernet implementation and test structure.
sources.apply: Reuse an understood MAC/PHY boundary and retain its attribution. Your contribution is the parser, state, fault handling, integration, and evidence.

sources.title: Taxi Transport Library
sources.highlight: Taxi provides SystemVerilog transport components and cocotb/Verilator tests. Its license choices differ from the old MIT-licensed repositories.
sources.apply: Check compatibility, board support, and redistribution requirements before selecting it. A newer library is not automatically a drop-in KR260 design.

sources.title: AddressSanitizer
sources.highlight: Instrumentation detects memory access and lifetime faults, including out-of-bounds reads and writes.
sources.apply: Run the C++ codec/replay tests with sanitizer instrumentation. Also compare protocol semantics against independent vectors, which memory checking cannot validate.

sources.title: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
sources.highlight: The undefined group covers signed overflow and invalid shifts, but excludes unsigned overflow and implicit conversions.
sources.apply: Widen before arithmetic and use explicit bounds checks. Make sanitizer findings fail tests; intentional sequence wrap needs a documented exception, not globally disabled checks.

sources.title: How the Internet Works
sources.highlight: The series builds intuition for Ethernet and the layers above it.
sources.apply: Watch the Ethernet/IP introduction, then annotate a real packet capture and write a one-page byte layout. Keep the exercise attached to the parser milestone.
